newsitem.title: UK: British unions must be positive under Labour - TUC.
newsitem.headline: British unions must be positive under Labour - TUC.

text.p: Britain's trade unions will need to develop a more constructive outlook if they want to influence a Labour Party government, the country's top unionist said in a New Year message on Sunday.

John Monks, general secretary of the Trades Union Congress (TUC), said unions could not count on any favours from Labour if the opposition party becomes the government next year. Labour's close ties to the unions have been loosened since Tony Blair was elected its leader in 1994.

"Britain desperately needs a new government, but a Labour election will only be the beginning of a new set of challenges for the trade union movement. There will be no cavalry coming over the hill to rescue us," Monks said.
Judging by opinion polls, Labour will win the next election, due by May 1997, and take power from a Conservative government that has passed a series of anti-union laws since 1979.
Labour is pledged to introduce a minimum wage and give unions greater recognition rights in the workplace, but it has refused to repeal the Conservatives' union laws.
Membership of the unions grouped in the TUC has halved to below seven million since the mid-1970s.
Monks said "habits of opposition" would have to be broken if the unions were to regain influence.

"But I am determined that we must move from being seen as part of the problem -- however unfairly -- to being part of the solution, working both to improve the lot of those at work and to make the country more prosperous and competitive," he said.

Monks, who has helped restore the unions' credibility since becoming TUC leader in 1993, repeated his call for partnership with industry, listing the creation of "positive working relationships with employers" as a union priority.
